html:
Cyclone Freddy was the longest-lasting tropical cyclone on record, which crossed the Indian Ocean in February and March 2023 and flooded southern Malawi. It formed off Australia and struck Madagascar and Mozambique twice before its rains reached Malawi.

In Malawi, mudslides and floods buried homes in and around Blantyre, killing over a thousand people and leaving hundreds of thousands homeless. It came a year after another storm, and during a cholera outbreak.

The disaster showed how exposed Malawi is to storms and floods as the climate warms, with deforested hills and crowded towns. It followed a pattern of cyclones hitting the region, as Cyclone Idai did in 2019, and as floods did in Mozambique in 2000.
